title: Fixed Leading Edge Access Panel — Installation and Water Ingress Check

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: Installation of a fixed leading edge access panel with the torque sequence, the seal seating check and the gutter flood test that proves water cannot reach the rib flange.

sections.purpose: This task installs an access panel on the fixed leading edge, seats the seal correctly and proves by a flood test that the joint keeps water out of the structure behind it.
sections.job_setup_note: The flood test needs about ten litres of water and a way of catching it at the drain; do not do it over a hangar floor without a tray. On aircraft with the moulded seal the panel must be pulled down evenly or the seal will roll out of its groove on one side and the leak will be at the corner furthest from where you are standing. Where the panel has been off for less than twenty-four hours and neither the seal nor the land was disturbed, the flood test may be omitted at the discretion of the certifying staff.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the slat supports are still fitted. 2. Clean the panel land and the seal groove and remove any old sealant. 3. Where the moulded seal is fitted, seat it in the groove all round and check that it is not stretched at the corners. 4. Where the sealant bead is used, apply it to the section given in the illustration and confirm that the drain hole is clear before the bead is laid. 5. Lift the panel onto the aperture with two people and start the centre fasteners first. CAUTION: PULL THE PANEL DOWN EVENLY FROM THE CENTRE OUTWARDS. A PANEL PULLED DOWN AT ONE END WILL ROLL THE SEAL OUT OF ITS GROOVE AT THE OTHER. 6. Where the bonded anchor nut strip is fitted, check that no anchor nut is turning before it is loaded. 7. Torque every fastener in the marked sequence, in two passes, to the value in the limits table. 8. Where the bracket kit D5720111574269 was disturbed, refit it and torque it before the panel is finally tightened. 9. Confirm that the skin panel D5720113135325 sits flush at the forward edge within the step limit. 10. Do the flood test: pour water into the leading edge gutter above the panel and let it run for ten minutes. 11. WARNING: KEEP WATER AWAY FROM THE ANTI-ICE DUCT JOINTS AND FROM ANY OPEN CONNECTOR. 12. Examine the rib flange behind the panel after ten minutes and confirm that it is dry. 13. Confirm that the drain, where fitted, is passing water and that the moulded drain fitting stands proud of the sealant land. 14. Remove the slat supports and retract the slats.
sections.close_out: Record the torque pass, the seal type fitted, and the flood test result and rib flange condition where the test was done. Where the flange is wet, do not release the panel; the seal has not seated and refitting it later will not fix it.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; steps 3, 6 and 13 apply only post modification

safety_precautions: Keep the slat supports fitted until the task is complete.
Keep water away from the anti-ice duct joints.
Two people are needed to lift the panel.

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: Installation of a fixed leading edge access panel with the torque sequence, the seal seating check and the gutter flood test that proves water cannot reach the rib flange.

sections.purpose: This task installs an access panel on the fixed leading edge, seats the seal correctly and proves by a flood test that the joint keeps water out of the structure behind it.
sections.job_setup_note: The flood test needs about ten litres of water and a way of catching it at the drain; do not do it over a hangar floor without a tray. On aircraft with the moulded seal the panel must be pulled down evenly or the seal will roll out of its groove on one side and the leak will be at the corner furthest from where you are standing. Where the panel has been off for less than twenty-four hours and neither the seal nor the land was disturbed, the flood test may be omitted at the discretion of the certifying staff. That discretion does not extend to a land carrying a recorded repair. A bushed insert or a local land doubler leaves the groove locally proud or locally distorted, often by less than half a millimetre, and the flood test is the only step in this task that will find it: the torque pass will read correct and the step check at the forward edge will pass. On a repaired land the test is done every time the panel is refitted, without exception.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the slat supports are still fitted. 2. Check the panel map for a recorded repair at any land on this panel and note it on the work card; a repaired land makes step 10 mandatory. 3. Clean the panel land and the seal groove and remove any old sealant. 4. Where the moulded seal is fitted, seat it in the groove all round and check that it is not stretched at the corners. Over a bushed insert, check that the groove floor is flush and that the seal is not lifted by the insert flange. 5. Where the sealant bead is used, apply it to the section given in the illustration and confirm that the drain hole is clear before the bead is laid. 6. Lift the panel onto the aperture with two people and start the centre fasteners first. CAUTION: PULL THE PANEL DOWN EVENLY FROM THE CENTRE OUTWARDS. A PANEL PULLED DOWN AT ONE END WILL ROLL THE SEAL OUT OF ITS GROOVE AT THE OTHER. 7. Where the bonded anchor nut strip is fitted, check that no anchor nut is turning before it is loaded. 8. Torque every fastener in the marked sequence, in two passes, to the value in the limits table. Where the bracket kit D5720111574269 was disturbed, refit it and torque it before the panel is finally tightened. 9. Confirm that the skin panel D5720113135325 sits flush at the forward edge within the step limit. 10. Do the flood test: pour water into the leading edge gutter above the panel and let it run for ten minutes. WARNING: KEEP WATER AWAY FROM THE ANTI-ICE DUCT JOINTS AND FROM ANY OPEN CONNECTOR. 11. Examine the rib flange behind the panel after ten minutes and confirm that it is dry. On a repaired land, examine the flange directly beneath the repaired position first; that is where a distorted groove leaks. 12. Confirm that the drain, where fitted, is passing water and that the moulded drain fitting stands proud of the sealant land. 13. Remove the slat supports and retract the slats.
sections.close_out: Record the torque pass, the seal type fitted, the repaired lands noted at step 2, the flood test result and the rib flange condition after the test. On a panel with a repaired land the flood test result is a mandatory entry and the panel may not be certified without it. Where the flange is wet, do not release the panel; the seal has not seated and refitting it later will not fix it.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; steps 4, 7 and 12 apply only post modification, and step 10 is mandatory on any panel with a recorded land repair

safety_precautions: Keep the slat supports fitted until the task is complete.
Keep water away from the anti-ice duct joints.
Two people are needed to lift the panel.
